Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
443 AM EDT Mon Mar 23 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No Significant changes to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Cold front and wave of low pressure depart today.

2) A series of frontal systems likely for the end of 
the week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Rain associated with a cold frontal passage and wave of low
pressure will continue to move across the area early this
morning and depart during the afternoon/evening. 

Expect rain to continue this morning, with POPs gradually
decreasing this afternoon. Much of this precipitation is now
post frontal with the cold front currently just south of Long
Island. As the precipitation comes to an end and some colder
temperatures move into the area, can not rule out some wet
snowflakes mixed in with the rain. The best chances for any wet
snowflakes will be across the far northern and northwestern
parts of the CWA. No accumulation is expected. 


.KEY MESSAGE 2... 
After a period of high pressure and a slight warming trend thru
Wednesday, a weak frontal passage is possible Wednesday night 
into Thursday. This front is moisture starved so not much in 
the way of precip is expected at this time. A cold front is then 
currently timed for late Thursday into Fri. Moisture transport 
ahead of the system could allow for a round of rain with the 
frontal passage. Temps behind the front likely to cool into the
40s for highs, with widespread subfreezing temps for lows.

&&

.AVIATION /08Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
A cold front and wave of low pressure will continue to move 
across the area early this morning and depart during the 
afternoon/evening. High pressure builds back into the region
tonight.

Conditions have been variable, from VFR to IFR, across the
region as a wave of low pressure tracks through the area. IFR to
LIFR becomes widespread this morning and into the early push as
another round of rain moves into the terminals.

Conditions gradually improve back to MVFR by mid to late morning,
into the mid afternoon, north and west to south and east as 
rain ends. A brief mix of rain/snow is possible at KSWF and KGON
as the precipitation ends. Improvement to VFR occurs during the
mid to late afternoon. There is timing uncertainty with the 
improving conditions and will be dependent on how quickly the 
low and cold front move south and east.

Winds NE 5 to 10 kt gradually back to N and increase early this
morning. During the afternoon, winds back to NNW with gusts 
17-24 kt. Occasional gusts 15-19 kt possible in the late 
morning. Gusts likely continue into evening at most terminals 
with gusts ending by late tonight.


 NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty... 

Amendments likely to refine timing of rain and flight category
changes into this morning.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z TUESDAY THROUGH FRIDAY... 

Late Monday night - Tuesday: VFR.

Wednesday: Mainly VFR with S/SW wind gusts 15-20 kt.

Thursday: VFR with a slight chance of rain in the evening, MVFR
or lower late at night with rain likely. SW wind gusts 15-20 
kt.

Friday: Chance of rain early with MVFR or lower possible. NW
wind gusts 15-20 kt.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
SCA conditions are expected on the waters today and tonight with
seas around 5 ft and gusts around 25kt. For the NON-ocean 
waters, winds and seas are expected to remain below SCA levels 
thru tonight. High pressure then builds in for the middle of the
week should keep winds and seas below SCA criteria for all 
waters thru the day on Thursday. Winds and seas ramp up Thursday
night thru Friday with a frontal system. Winds and seas 
expected to fall below SCA levels on Sat attm.

&&
